sources.title: Paolo Sartori and Yuri Bregel, Khiva, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read. Capital under Arab Muhammad I, seventeenth-century irrigation, coerced labor, slavery and royal archive. Qonghrat rulers assumed khan title in 1804; imported 1783 endpoint is not a fall date.

sources.title: C. E. Bosworth, Chorasmia ii: In Islamic Times, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct read, final four historical paragraphs. Arabshahid establishment 1511; Nader 1740; 1873 protectorate and February 1920 overthrow. Older entry gives approximate dynastic decline; more recent Khiva article informs detailed capital phase.

sources.title: Yuri Bregel, Bigar, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct read. Khiva-specific paragraph distinguishes government main-canal qazu from community sub-canal work. General labor burdens vary widely, so no region-wide day count is imposed on Khiva households.

sources.title: Bertold Spuler, Abu’l-Ghazi Bahador Khan, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct read. Isfahan study, Chaghatay works and Shajara-yi Tarakima dated 1659 to 1660. Do not reproduce the erroneous 1076/1655 conversion or obsolete personal attribution of the continuation to Anusha; Toshov supplies newer manuscript research.

sources.title: TDV Islam Ansiklopedisi, Şecere-i Terâkime
sources.note: Direct HTML heading reads شجرۂ تراكمه. This is scholarly Arabic-script typography for a historical Chaghatay title, not a visual reading of an autograph. English translation follows the work identification in Spuler. Only two source-script words reproduced.

sources.title: Nuryoghdi Toshov, The Earliest Copy of the Shajara-yi Turk: An Autograph?, Austrian Academy of Sciences
sources.note: Direct Russian original research read. MS Tashkent 851, inserted folios 84a to 86b, marginal continuation on 83b, coauthor statement on 185b, teacher identification and provisional autograph hypothesis. Article text checked; manuscript figures not independently deciphered.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Itchan Kala
sources.note: Direct institutional statement read, Outstanding Universal Value: domestic courtyards, reception porticoes and private rooms; eighteenth- and twentieth-century variants; later monuments. Current heritage description does not date every surviving house to early khanate.

sources.title: ICOMOS, Itchan Kala evaluation, nomination 543
sources.note: Direct original PDF read, English printed pages 38 to 39, human PDF pages 2 to 3. Djuma rebuilt 1788 to 1789, reused elements; Alla-Kuli madrasa 1835 beside east gate and market. Conflicting 112/212 column totals within the document are omitted, as are its inaccurate political chronology and unverified architect execution story.

sources.title: Dodo Nazilov, The Interior and Space Outside, San’at 2008 no. 3, Academy of Arts of Uzbekistan
sources.note: Direct author article read. Khiva ulu-aivan faces lower aivan, rises above house, directs prevailing wind into courtyard. Study of traditional surviving architecture; no exact invention date assigned.

sources.title: Austrian Academy of Sciences, Central Asia Melons in Hungary? Ónody’s Journey to Khiva (1875)
sources.note: Full indexed original article read; direct extraction initially cache-missed. Sections on September 1875 audience, local agricultural guide, 1877 publications and commercially unsuccessful seeds. Traveler’s prejudiced ethnic judgments not adopted. Explicitly later than map coverage.

proposedOverrides.name: Khiva Khanate
proposedOverrides.summary: A Khorezm oasis state shaped by irrigation, scholarship and changing dynasties.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact uncovered index record checked. Map interval 1530 to 1783; decoded polygon bounds about 50.327 to 70.095 E, 36.307 to 45.977 N, nearly unchanged across multiple snapshots. No modern national outline inferred. Historical Arabshahid state begins 1511, Khiva capital under Arab Muhammad I 1603 to 1622, Qonghrat khan title from 1804, protectorate 1873, monarchy ends 1920. Period 1603 is circa because capital shift is dated within the reign. No association with Bukhara.
